correctness.rationale: For a fixed tree the sole nonzero peak/trough indicator interactions occur at distances zero, one and two. Same-site exclusion and two exact beta integrals yield H_1 and H_2. A weighted Cayley forest polynomial gives the conditioned multinomial-plus-Bernoulli degrees for one edge and one 2-edge path, with respective incidences 2/n and 3/n^2. Summing ordered pairs gives the exact finite formula. Binomial/multinomial Poisson convergence yields the displayed constant. Its negative sign is certified by a rational interval for the Poisson(1) distribution truncated to 0..10 and a total-variation tail bound 21T. check.py passed 373 exact assertions, including complete tree enumeration through n=6 and finite rank permutations where indicated. This proves only averaged conditional covariance, not unconditional covariance or concentration.

originality.rationale: The stated claim is a negative linear limit of the *tree-averaged conditional* maximum/minimum count covariance on uniformly random labeled trees, together with its exact finite-size degree-pair formula and a path contrast. Searches covered aliases such as peaks, troughs, local extrema, landscapes, random labeling, and conditioned spanning-tree degrees. Majumdar--Martin (2006) computes minima statistics for fixed geometry; Clark (2005) uses internal rooted path extrema, a different statistic; Burdzy--Pal (2016) conditions on one or two peaks; Diaz-Lopez et al. (2017) enumerate fixed-graph peak sets and use a distinct degree-one convention. The inspected statements do not directly imply the uniformly random tree-averaged mixed covariance or its negative asymptotic coefficient. This remains a same-model and non-exhaustive priority assessment: implicit consequences of general enumerators are possible.
residual_risks: General peak-set enumeration or random-graph landscape generating functions may contain the result implicitly even if not stated in inspected sections.

value.rationale: Local maxima and minima are the natural paired critical-point counts in independent random energy landscapes. Their dependence is locally competitive (same vertex, distance-two) and cooperative (adjacency); determining the sign after averaging a random tree geometry is not a separate-marginal or routine fixed-degree count. The exact signed locality formula, forest-conditioned degree law and rigorously negative asymptotic coefficient solve a meaningful quenched-dependence question. Positive covariance for paths of order >=5 makes the topology dependence explicit. The quantity is a complete well-defined observable of random labeled trees, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
